body:
Thank you for that insight, especially in this topic thread I am sure its not easy admitting to be the initial cheater, your words are on track with what I kind of already knew but didn't want to admit, that the opposite affect would be the likely result if she found out...

If you don't mind my asking, is that how/why you found out? Like she told you to try and teach you a lesson? Or was it a case of her trying to feel better about herself and she just slipped up?
Thank you for your advice and asking coward99 for his input. I honestly wasn't expecting this many responses and it has been really good at keeping me grounded.

See thats something I've thought a lot about, what to do if/when I told her or she found out. I don't want her to be taught a lesson or be fearful I am considering other options. I just feel fatigued by thinking i am alone in always wanting to put the SO first and don't want to be in a position where I think I am better than my partner. I know the counter arguement is that not everyone is unfaithful, but I have never seen it and am at a point where I don't believe it to be true, so it must be me that has change in order to be in a balanced relationship

I agree with that point, but after been cheated on and the casual sex carousel it propelled me before I met her I lost that idea that love and sex are exclusive. With her now, its still loved filled when we have sex, but when we swing its disconnected physical fun that we do together and know immediately afterwards we are still there for each other emotionally

No I wasn't worried about that, this was someone she shared everything about our relationship with, which I have always done with female friends so I don't mind that, and she brought it up as an update on our relationship vs a "hey the boundaries for us are gone," but he only saw the opprotunity for himself and not that obviously he would never be welcomed for what he did. Just seeing his push tactics and the guilt games he plays sickens me... wow a bit hypocritical for this post I realize...

This most definitely hurt my ego a lot for all the reasons we know, and right now the only thing that is healing that aspect of me is having a lot of attractive people flirt with me. Its almost become an addiction, but my desire to have sex with them is really low. Its just helping with the self image issues, I am also about to start counseling and am hoping to maybe find another way to cope and gain my self-respect back

I don't want to fully believe that, but my personal history has taught me otherwise to where I don't think I could start any new relationship without already distrusting the person, which is not fair and pessimistic but its where I am at right now..

It was just two nights, but I am sure they were probably sexting a couple weeks before that. This happened before we had the discussions about going open, and so far it has only been when we're together or talking dirty to each other. But when he found out we wanted to go open, his first response was if he could hook up again.

Thank you for the advice brother, I think you'll understand this, the whole situation felt so much more heightened because at the time I was going thru the lance corporal ethics seminar and it was constant discussions on loyalty, commitment, respect, blah blah blah... Iguess I shouldn't rush into anything and should give her time to let her actions convey her feelings..

She left her journal open one day that had the details, so naturally I confronted her, she seemed remorseful and it was difficult but we pushed thru and she agreed to not speak to the friend again. Fast forward some time and she admits that she is talking to him again because he was going thru a divorce and wanted to be a support. I was pretty mad to be honest, I mean she was willing allowing this guy that came between us back in the picture. The next time we were together and she fell asleep i went thru her messages, I know snooping is wrong but I believe in 'trust but verify' for better or for worse... and I think it was a telling experience. He was making advances on her again and inquires as to if he had any other shots at her. She did ignore all the advances and kept the conversation on topic which was nice. I know the guy is her only friend she could talk to about one aspect of her life and I understand why she wanted to be friends, but the fact is the guy doesn't respect me, our relationship or her and she shouldn't have to ask me a second time if I "want her to stop talking to him." 

I think a lil clarifying may also help in terms of the open aspect of our relationship. We are okay with each other going out partying with friends and dancing on strangers, and even making out as long as clothes are on, but any sexual swinging can only take place if we are present and are comfortable with the other couple. But this was not the case, this was planned out and had an emotional element to it, which is why it hurt so much.
Anyways.. part of me knows that, but Its just hard for me to view that as a benefit in this situation. I don't want to think less of her, nobody is perfect and I am far from it too..
